subject: Wellspan Dedicated capacity: throughput -> commit pathway
messages:
From: Keith Milburn <keith.milburn@wellspanhealth.org>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing question - initial metrics attached

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send our high-level traffic picture so we can get an initial sizing and committed capacity estimate from Redwood. Attached is a CSV export from our gateway with last-30-days aggregates, but here are the headline numbers:

- Total requests/day (all endpoints): ~120,000
- Typical working hours spike (09:00-17:00 ET): ~180k/day concentrated
- Average request context length: 1,024 tokens (includes system + user + messages)
- Average response length: ~220 tokens
- Peak sustained QPS (burst windows): 220 QPS for 10–15 minutes
- Typical baseline concurrency observed: ~35–45 concurrent user sessions; spikes up to ~78 concurrent generator sessions
- Model mix: 70% text-gen (single-turn + multi-turn summarization), 30% embeddings + reranking
- Latency target: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms (we can relax p99 if needed, but procurement will push for p95 guarantees)

Questions for Redwood:
1) What dedicated pool configuration would you recommend to meet the latency targets and handle the peak QPS with good headroom?
2) What reserved commit terms (12 vs 24 months) make sense given this workload and what discounts apply?
3) How do you price burst capacity vs guaranteed baseline?
4) Any suggestions to reduce unit cost (quantization, batching, KV caching) we should prioritize?

Please loop in whoever owns sizing/planning — procurement wants an indicative monthly cost and showback figures for our cloud team.

Thanks,
Keith
VP Engineering, Wellspan Health

Attachments: wellspan-workload-metrics.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Keith Milburn <keith.milburn@wellspanhealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing question - initial metrics attached

Keith — thanks for the numbers and the CSV. This is exactly the sort of data we need. A few quick clarifying questions before Ben (capacity planning) gives a sizing recommendation: 

- Are the 220 QPS bursts dominated by short requests (<= 256 tokens) or by long transcripts? The CSV looks mixed but I want to confirm.
- How tolerant are you to p95 vs p99 tradeoffs for the embedding/reranking path? Can embedding calls be batched with slightly higher latency budget?
- Do you expect traffic growth over the next 6 months (20–40% typical) or is this a fairly stable operational load?

From a packaging standpoint: we typically propose a baseline dedicated pool sized for steady-state concurrency with an autoscaling buffer for short burst windows. If you share the CSV column mapping for request sizes I’ll ask Ben to run it through our throughput model and send an indicative H100/A100 pool recommendation + commit pricing (12 vs 24 months) later tomorrow.

I’ve looped in Ben (PM, Dedicated) who will outline the GPU mix, estimated throughput, and the reserved commit tiers we can offer.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Keith Milburn <keith.milburn@wellspanhealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:00:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing question - initial metrics attached

Thanks for the data — I ran the CSV through our workload simulator with the model-mix you described. Below is the recommendation and rationale (high level):

Summary recommendation (initial, conservative):
- Dedicated pool: 8 x NVIDIA H100 80GB (private pool, single-tenant)
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~65 QPS for large-context gen (1,000–1,200 tokens avg) + ~35 QPS for embeddings/rerank when batched => ~100 QPS sustained with headroom
- Burst handling: autoscaling policy to add up to 2 additional H100s for 10–20 minute windows (handles the 220 QPS short bursts with graceful degradation)
- Concurrency sizing: target pool to support 48 concurrent generation sessions at p95 latency < 200ms for the primary model (70B quantized path)

Key assumptions used in model:
- Primary text-gen model is quantized to 4-bit with optimized kernels (KV cache hit rate ~18% across sessions).
- Average generation latency per token on H100 80GB kernel stack ~1.8 ms (model/sequence dependent).
- Embeddings path uses mixed-precision and batched calls (batch sizes 32–64) for throughput efficiency.

Pricing & commit guidance (indicative):
- On-demand dedicated pool pricing: $X,XXX per GPU-hour (noted below as baseline for transparency).
- 12-month reserved commit discount: ~22% off list dedicated rate (applies to baseline pool hours; burst autoscaling billed at on-demand rate).
- 24-month reserved commit discount: ~30% off list; includes 10% reserved credits for burst minutes (effectively reduces on-demand burst cost).
- Baseline sizing we recommend for purchase: reserve 8 GPUs. Recommend a 12-month commit as the baseline for quicker procurement; 24-month if you want deeper discounts and a capex-like predictable unit cost.

Cost example (monthly estimates, ballpark):
- Reserve 8 x H100 (12-month): ~$95,000/month (after ~22% commitment discount applied to baseline hours)
- Burst usage (estimated 15 hours/month across scaling windows): additional ~$3,400 (on-demand)
- One-time onboarding + runbook drafting: $12,000 (optional; includes model pinning, canary rollout config, and KV-cache tuning)

Ways to reduce unit cost:
- Quantize heavier models to 3-bit where feasible (saves 20–30% inference cost with modest quality tradeoffs)
- Increase batching for embeddings calls (client-side aggregation windows of 100–200 ms) to lower per-vector cost
- Enable prefix/KV caching aggressively for long multi-turn sessions

SLA points: our standard Dedicated SLA includes 99.9% availability for the pool and SLOs for model invocation p95 latency; tighter latency-based financial credits can be negotiated as part of an enterprise addendum.

I’ll attach a short spreadsheet that shows how throughput maps to GPU counts for different model sizes — Marissa can follow up with a formal proposal PDF with tiered pricing and negotiated discount line items.

— Ben Carter
Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Keith Milburn <keith.milburn@wellspanhealth.org>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Redwood Dedicated proposal (v2) - Wellspan (inc. committed discount options)

Keith, team — attaching the formal proposal (see redwood-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf attached). Key points pulled out here so procurement can take to legal: 

- Baseline commitment: 8 x H100 (80GB) reserved for 12 months at 22% discount off list for dedicated baseline hours.
- Optional 24-month commitment: 30% discount; includes 10% reserved burst credits that lower effective on-demand price for autoscale minutes.
- Pricing mechanics: baseline billed as monthly committed GPU-hours; burst scaled minutes billed at on-demand unit prices; any sustained above-burst usage converts to overage at on-demand rates unless renegotiated.
- SLA / credits: 99.9% pool availability standard. We can add a latency SLO appendix (p95 credit ladder) for enterprise deals — we typically require a 12–24 week onboarding to instrument latency SLOs and create the tracing hooks.
- Evaluation windows: we can set a 60-day performance acceptance window after initial onboarding; if performance materially deviates we offer a separation credit or a model-tuning engagement to remediate.

Concessions we can offer today to help close: 
- One-time 10% onboarding credit on the first month (applied to the invoice)
- For a signed 12-month commitment this quarter, we can move to 24% discount (additional 2% from standard 22%) — requires SOC 2 evidence package within 30 days.
- Standard procurement doc set (SOC 2, data flow diagram, encryption whitepaper) is attached as a drive link in the proposal.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement reviews the PDF and confirms if the 12-month at 24% concession is acceptable.
2) Legal to review SLA appendix and redline (we can fast-track).
3) Schedule kickoff (1 hour) with Ben and infra to confirm autoscale knobs and DR plan.

Marissa Cole
Head — Customer Solutions (Americas)
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf
From: Keith Milburn <keith.milburn@wellspanhealth.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@wellspanhealth.org
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated proposal (v2) - Wellspan (inc. committed discount options)

Marissa / Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Procurement reviewed the PDF this morning; high-level notes:

- The 12-month at 24% looks acceptable to the business. Procurement needs the following clarified before routing to legal:
  * Exact monthly committed dollar amount (line item) for accounting (not just per-GPU placeholders)
  * Confirmation that burst minutes will be itemized separately on invoices (we need a cap/alert threshold)
  * SLA appendix: we will want a p95 latency ladder included in the contract (financial credits on missed p95).

We are comfortable moving forward with a kickoff if Redwood can confirm the above items and provide the SOW + final invoice line. Also please include a note on migration rollback strategy in case the integration impacts downstream EHR latency.

If you can update the proposal with those line items I’ll route to legal and procurement (we’re trying to finish before month-end).

Best,
Keith
VP Engineering, Wellspan Health
